page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Top: running text paragraph in roman type. Then an ornamental fleuron rule. Then a centred title block in capitals and italic subtitle, a sequence of numbered theses (Roman numerals) each followed by an italic thesis, with a fleuron-free layout. Bottom: signature "B 3" at left and catchword "VI. Quia" at right.

main_text.p: tamen canes venatici ita instituuntur, ut visâ perdice subsistant, & auditô displosionis strepitu accurrant; Quanquàm verò bestiæ ratione careát & forte omni cogitatione, omnes tamen motus spirituum & conarij, qui excitant in nobis passiones, in illis quoq; sunt, ut inserviant motibus nervorum & musculorum excitandis, cóservandis & confirmandis, qui motus in nobis comitari solent passiones; Hactenus de passionibus mentis in genere.
main_text.head: COLLECTANEA EX UNIVERSA Cartesii Philosophia.

p.i: Mens est substantia cogitans; Corpus verò substantia extensa.
Unio mentis cum corpore est unum ex primò notis.
Cognoscitur sensibus tantùm; Ut proinde intellectus eam non assequatur.
Mentis à corpore separatæ cœlum sunt gloriosissima cogitationes de Deo.

page.notes: The fleuron rule is an ornament, not text; it is marked as a row of symbols. The thesis numbers I to IV are set as separate lines and kept as paragraphs. The opening "V." thesis and "VI. Quia" appear only in the catchword area; the catchword is taken from the foot of the page. Some letters in the italic theses are faint and read with reasonable confidence.
